interpretations: Long film means length > 112 (strictly greater); the average length and the average of replacement_cost/rental_rate are computed over those films.
Long film means length >= 112 (inclusive of 112); the same two averages are computed over those films.
The ratio is the mean of per-film ratios (AVG(replacement_cost / rental_rate)), not total replacement cost divided by total rental rate.
The ratio is the ratio of the two group averages (AVG(replacement_cost) / AVG(rental_rate)), not the mean of per-film ratios.
The ratio is rental_rate / replacement_cost, the inverse of the stated order (unlikely, since the question states replacement_cost / rental_rate).
The average running time is the AVG(length) over long films, in minutes, unrounded.
Films with NULL length are excluded, since they cannot be classed as long.

Films with NULL length are excluded from the group but films with NULL rental_rate or replacement_cost remain in the group, and the ratio average skips them (rental_rate and replacement_cost are NOT NULL, so there is no practical effect).
Rental_rate of zero would give a division error or NULL for the ratio; it is treated as missing, though the data shows only 0.99, 2.99 and 4.99.
The result is one row with two columns: average length first, average ratio second.
The result is one row with a single group over all long films, not broken down by rating, category, store or any other grouping.
The long-film group is taken from the film table alone, not restricted to films with inventory copies, rentals or payments.
The long-film group is restricted to films that have inventory copies, with the averages weighted by copy count (each inventory row counted once).
The averages are over distinct films in the film table, not over rentals or inventory rows.
Film length is read from film.length, not from film_text, which has no length column.
The average is returned unrounded, as full-precision floating-point values.
If no film exceeds the cutoff, both values are NULL.
Missing interpretations:

Long film means length > 112, so films with length exactly 112 are excluded. The existing list treats this as a boundary choice, but it never says the cutoff of 112 itself is a threshold and not a data value (this is the same as the first interpretation, so it adds nothing new).
The only genuinely missing readings are these:
The "average of each film's replacement cost divided by its rental rate" is computed with integer or truncated division, not decimal division (not applicable here because both columns are DECIMAL).
The long-film cutoff is applied to a length converted to another unit, such as hours, instead of minutes (not applicable here because the question states 112 minutes).
Films are grouped by the cutoff into long and not long, and the result is only the long group's row, with no row for the short group.
Films with a NULL ratio, caused by a NULL or zero rental_rate, are excluded from the ratio average only, and they still count in the average length.
queries: SELECT AVG(length), AVG(replacement_cost / rental_rate) FROM film WHERE length > 112
SELECT AVG(rental_rate), AVG(replacement_cost) FROM film WHERE length >= 112
SELECT rating, AVG(replacement_cost) / AVG(rental_rate) AS ratio FROM film GROUP BY rating
SELECT AVG(length) FROM film WHERE length > 120
